text:
ravi: Observed a weird p95/p99 jump on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate. p50 is stable, but tail latency up ~80-200ms in the last hour.
ben: Can you paste the console query or a screenshot? curious if this is a sampling/origin change :eyes:
maya: We had a routing weight change this morning for the cost-optimized variant — could be that. Also some tenants hit quota fallbacks around 14:10.
ravi: Query I used: `measure(latency_ms) by (endpoint, model_variant) where endpoint=\"/v1/generate\" window=1h`
ben: If median is flat but p99 jumps, small subpopulation shift or cache effect likely. Check `token_count` and `cache_hit` tags.
sophie: UX note: it's really tough to tell from the legend whether the chart mix changed due to routing vs fallback. A small origin badge for routing weight changes would help :thinking:
deploy-bot: rollout-service updated weights: model-variant-b -> 15% (from 0%) at 2026-03-22T14:12:05Z
ravi: That timestamp aligns with when the p95 rises. But p50 not affected — suggests the slow variant is responsible for tail only.
maya: Hypothesis: model-variant-b has slower KV-cache warmup or different batching path. Recommend splitting the rollup by `cache_hit` and `request_length`.
ben: Can someone run a quick aggregate? `select percentile(latency_ms,95), count(*) from traces where endpoint=\"/v1/generate\" group by model_variant, cache_hit`
ravi: Pasted results: model-a p95=110ms count=12,400; model-b p95=320ms count=1,820; model-b cache_hit=false p95=420ms count=600
sophie: So model-b cache misses are dominating the tail. UX ask: add quick toggles to show `sample-origin` and `cache_hit` breakdown in the latency pane.
maya: Also propose automatic chart annotations when routing or weight changes occur so historical percentiles show the context (e.g., "routing weight changed: +15% model-b").
ben: Filed a tiny dashboard ticket: https://redwood.internal/issue/PLAT-983 — will add sample toggles and an annotation framework for rollout events.
ravi: Thanks — I'll keep monitoring the rolling window. If p99 doesn't improve we should revert the weight.
ai-ops-bot: alert: routing-weight anomaly detected and automatically reverted at 2026-03-22T15:02:40Z :white_check_mark:
sophie: Follow-up suggestion: tooltip copy explaining how percentiles can be sensitive to small subpopulations (short example + visual) so PMs don't misread these spikes.
ben: +1. Short explainer + example panels will reduce confusion.
